narrative.overview:
The page is the stage manager's call desk. One cue sits in standby at a time, its light beside the caption, and it is called with a single GO. Around it the desk stays dark: a blackout ground (the house is dark, the tab lives on a second monitor in a dark room), panels lit by blue work light, recessed wells a shade deeper for anything the user types or reads as raw text. Paper-white script text, blue-grey for everything that can wait.

The desk refuses the grey dashboard of equal panels. The decision and the conversation own the left column; the right column holds the quieter panels in the user's order of importance (tests, plans in progress, what to build next, connected sessions last). Colour is not decoration here: each cue colour has one fixed job, so a glance from the side reads the state without reading a word. Density is that of a working tool (13.5 to 14.5px body, 11px tracked captions); only the decision's summary is large.

Stillness is a material property of this world. Nothing re-renders under the pointer or the reading eye: the decision card is never replaced while it is read, a card that vanished stays as a tombstone, the conversation and the right column freeze while hovered. Dark only, flat, no drop shadows.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only: blackout ground, blue work-light panels, deeper wells.
Four cue colours with fixed jobs; tints derived by `color-mix()` against the panel.
One loud line (the 22px card summary); everything else is dense and quiet.
1px rails and tone separate surfaces; no elevation.
Authored 16x16 SVG icons at 1.5 stroke, CSS-drawn chevrons; no glyph icons.
French copy, keyboard-first: key digits printed on the controls.

rules.name: The Fixed Jobs Rule
rules.body: Green is go / OK / done and progress; amber is what waits on you (your decision, the recommendation, a session's context filling up); red is stop (approval, breakage, a session that must hand off and clear); blue is the away summary and nothing else. A colour never borrows another's job, and a new state picks the job it shares or stays neutral.

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Coloured text on a panel uses the ink tokens (Amber Ink, Red Ink); the fill tokens are for borders, dots, bars and filled buttons.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Every colour comes from the `:root` custom properties. Tints are `color-mix()` of a cue colour into the panel (10 to 12% for banner grounds, 40 to 70% for tinted borders), never new hex values.

rules.name: The One Loud Line Rule
rules.body: Only the card summary is large. Panel captions stay 11px tracked caps in House Grey so the summary is the only thing the eye lands on from across the room.

rules.name: The Caption Not Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Tracked caps name a panel or sit inline beside content (Proposition, recommandé); nothing sits in caps above a title. The card's nature goes on the meta line under the summary.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Times, counts and ratios that update in place use `tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Priority Order Rule
rules.body: The page order is the user's order of importance: decision, conversation, tests (OK / Pas OK / Clarifier), plans in progress, what to build next, connected sessions last and pinned. A new block takes its rank in that list, never the top by default.

rules.name: The Still Page Rule
rules.body: Nothing re-renders under the pointer or the reading eye. The card is never replaced while unanswered; a vanished card stays as a tombstone (dashed border, struck summary, muted cue) until dismissed; the conversation and the right column freeze while hovered or while a field inside has focus. Nothing auto-scrolls.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows, glows or blur. Separate surfaces by tone and 1px rails.

rules.name: The Cue Light Rule
rules.body: The lamp beside the title tells whether the keys answer: off while arming, green when live, red when the server is lost. Nothing else on the card blinks or moves.

rules.name: The Drawn Icon Rule
rules.body: Icons are authored inline SVG on a 16x16 grid, 1.5 stroke, round caps, `currentColor`, 12px rendered; chevrons are CSS-drawn. Never a Unicode glyph as an icon.

dos: **Do** keep the page dark only: Blackout ground, Work-light Panel surfaces, Well Blue for anything typed or literal.
**Do** give each cue colour its one job: green go / OK / done and progress, amber what waits on you, red stop (approval, breakage, a session to hand off), blue the away summary only.
**Do** derive tints with `color-mix()` against the panel and use the ink tokens for coloured text.
**Do** keep the card summary the only large text (22px/600) and every panel caption 11px tracked caps in House Grey.
**Do** double colour with shape in the session strip: round lives its own life, square waits on you.
**Do** print the key on the control it triggers (option digits, "(N)", the Entrée legend on GO); the hint line carries only what no control shows.
**Do** arm a new card before its keys answer (400ms, 800ms for an approval) and show it on the cue light.
**Do** use `tabular-nums` for times, counts and ratios.
donts: **Don't** add drop shadows, glows or elevation; separate by tone and 1px rails.
**Don't** re-render, replace, reflow or auto-scroll anything under the pointer or the reading eye; a vanished card becomes a tombstone, hovered columns freeze.
**Don't** put a caps eyebrow above a title.
**Don't** use a Unicode glyph as an icon; draw it in SVG.
**Don't** add a light theme or "new" badges; the away banner is the only catch-up.
**Don't** move a block above the decision card or out of the priority order.
